check.reason: Melian shares none of this text, which the reviewing host's store and terminal hold

snippet.text: `Lowering` holds one proposal against the fence, and `refusal()` says why it fails. It refuses a decision-model executor, a refuted verdict, a `melian/injection-attempt` claim, and a defect a deterministic check co-reported. It refuses a P0, a target of `nit`, and any move but one step down. It refuses a target the table in force resolves `silent`, a table Melian could not read, and a proposal with no evidence at the head. `VerificationRecord.refusal(report)` says why a later report of a claim cannot follow the stored one: it is taken only when none is stored, when it is the stored report again, as a replay sends it, or when its verdict is stronger, and it then replaces the stored report whole. Otherwise the first report stands, its reason and lowering included, as [the decision](../decisions/2026-11-28-a-claims-first-report-stands.md) sets out.

message.text: The rewritten line says `VerificationRecord.refusal(report)` takes a later report "only when none is stored, when it is the stored report again ... or when its verdict is stronger, and it then replaces the stored report whole. Otherwise the first report stands". The code at head takes a report in a fourth case too: `refusal` returns `undefined` for an equal or weaker report that answers `different` where the stored report did not (verification.ts:145-150). And `after` never replaces the stored report whole: it keeps any stored `different` answer through `withDifferent` (verification.ts:162).

Say that a stronger report replaces the stored one except for any stored `different` answer, and name `whole()` and `after()` beside `refusal()`.
explanation.whyHere: AGENTS.md says: "Update documentation in the same change whenever behaviour diverges from what is documented." This change edited this line and left it describing the first commit's rule, not the different-wins rule that 9f6a71f54 added in the same pull request. The core guideline is the document `packages/core/AGENTS.md` imports for anyone working on `VerificationRecord`, so this is a document stating behaviour the code no longer has.

properties.failureScenario: A contributor reads core.md line 413 and expects `new VerificationRecord({ verdict: "confirmed", matches: { d: "same" } }).refusal({ verdict: "confirmed", matches: { d: "different" } })` to return a refusal, since the report is neither a first report, a replay nor stronger. The code returns `undefined`, and `after` keeps the stored report with `matches.d` set to `different`. Going by the doc, a contributor might "fix" the code back to refusing, which would bring back the inherited-dismissal defect this PR fixes. They might also assume a stronger report's `same` answer overwrites a stored `different` ("replaces the stored report whole"), but `after` keeps `different`.

message.text: Step 17's line in the plan still says "equal verdicts keep the higher severity, with the winning report's reason and evidence, in the report's commit and on replay." This change replaces that rule. `upsertVerification` now throws `VerificationRecord.refusal`'s reason for any later report at an equal verdict that is not a replay and adds no `different` answer, so the first report stands whatever its severity. This is one of two stale statements in this plan step. The other is line 114, "A refused lowering still records the verdict.", reported separately.

- Done when, the tool: `report_verdict` takes a lower severity with a reason, and refuses one outside the fence. That is more than one step, a P0, or a result that is `nit` or that the table in force resolves `silent`. It is also an injection attempt, a deterministic co-report, or a `refuted` verdict. A refused lowering still records the verdict.

properties.failureScenario: A verifier reports claim c1 confirmed and lowered P1 to P2, then reports it confirmed again, unlowered. The plan says equal verdicts keep the higher severity, so a reader expects the claim back at P1 with the second report's reason. At head the second call is refused with "this claim is already judged confirmed, lowered P1 to P2, ...", and the claim stays at P2 with the first reason. A contributor who checks step 17 against the plan would read the new behaviour as a regression.

properties.failureScenario: A verifier calls `report_verdict` with `{ verdict: "confirmed", reason: "First try.", lower: { severity: "P2", ... } }` and no evidence. The plan promises the verdict is recorded with the lowering refused. At head the call throws "a lowering requires evidence locations at the head ...; nothing was recorded", and no verification is stored for the claim. A reader of the plan would expect the claim to be judged confirmed.
